title: Parse XML data with ElementTree
instruction:
Parse the XML string below using `xml.etree.ElementTree.fromstring()`. Then print each product's name and price, one per line, formatted as:

`Product: <name> — $<price>`

XML data:
```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<products>
  <product sku="WM-001">
    <name>Wireless Mouse</name>
    <price>29.99</price>
  </product>
  <product sku="KB-002">
    <name>Mechanical Keyboard</name>
    <price>89.99</price>
  </product>
</products>
```
starter_code:
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

xml_data = """<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<products>
  <product sku="WM-001">
    <name>Wireless Mouse</name>
    <price>29.99</price>
  </product>
  <product sku="KB-002">
    <name>Mechanical Keyboard</name>
    <price>89.99</price>
  </product>
</products>"""

# Parse the XML and print product info
solution_code:
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

xml_data = """<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<products>
  <product sku="WM-001">
    <name>Wireless Mouse</name>
    <price>29.99</price>
  </product>
  <product sku="KB-002">
    <name>Mechanical Keyboard</name>
    <price>89.99</price>
  </product>
</products>"""

root = ET.fromstring(xml_data)
for product in root.findall("product"):
    name = product.find("name").text
    price = product.find("price").text
    print(f"Product: {name} — ${price}")

test_cases.expected_output:
Product: Wireless Mouse — $29.99
Product: Mechanical Keyboard — $89.99

title: Build an XML payload for an API request
instruction:
Use `xml.etree.ElementTree` to build an XML document representing a new customer. The root element should be `<customer>`. Add these child elements:

- `<name>` with text "Alice"
- `<email>` with text "alice@example.com"
- `<age>` with text "28"

The `<customer>` element should have an attribute `type="premium"`.

Serialize to a string with `ET.tostring(root, encoding="unicode")` and print the result.
starter_code:
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

# Build the customer XML payload
solution_code:
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

root = ET.Element("customer")
root.set("type", "premium")

ET.SubElement(root, "name").text = "Alice"
ET.SubElement(root, "email").text = "alice@example.com"
ET.SubElement(root, "age").text = "28"

xml_output = ET.tostring(root, encoding="unicode")
print(xml_output)

title: Parse XML to a dictionary with xmltodict
instruction:
Use `xmltodict.parse()` to convert the XML string below into a Python dictionary. Then:

1. Print the user's name
2. Print the user's email
3. Print the user's role (from the `@role` attribute)

Each on its own line.

XML:
```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<user role="admin">
  <name>Charlie</name>
  <email>charlie@example.com</email>
</user>
```
starter_code:
import xmltodict

xml_data = """<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<user role="admin">
  <name>Charlie</name>
  <email>charlie@example.com</email>
</user>"""

# Parse and extract fields
solution_code:
import xmltodict

xml_data = """<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<user role="admin">
  <name>Charlie</name>
  <email>charlie@example.com</email>
</user>"""

data = xmltodict.parse(xml_data)
user = data["user"]
print(user["name"])
print(user["email"])
print(user["@role"])

title: Validate XML payload structure
instruction:

3. Checks that the root has an `id` attribute — if not, return `("Missing 'id' attribute", False)`
4. Checks that `<customer>` exists as a child — if not, return `("Missing 'customer'", False)`

title: Build an XML payload for an API request
instruction:
Build an XML string representing a product using `ET.SubElement()` and print the result.

The product should have:
- Root element: `<product>` with attribute `sku="TBL-001"`
- Child `<name>`: "Oak Table"
- Child `<price>`: "249.99"
- Child `<in_stock>`: "true"

Serialize with `ET.tostring(root, encoding="unicode")` and print the XML string.
starter_code:
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

# Build the product XML
solution_code:
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

root = ET.Element("product")
root.set("sku", "TBL-001")
ET.SubElement(root, "name").text = "Oak Table"
ET.SubElement(root, "price").text = "249.99"
ET.SubElement(root, "in_stock").text = "true"

xml_payload = ET.tostring(root, encoding="unicode")
print(xml_payload)
